summary: CCC-built 1940 steel lookout in Lewis County, NY; staffed 1941 to 1988, closed 1989, still standing and closed to the public because it holds radio gear.

facts.design: 67 ft 6 in International Derrick steel lookout tower
facts.status_note: Still standing and closed. NHLR says it holds numerous pieces of radio equipment; Wikipedia says it is used as an antenna support structure.

access.note: NHLR: the site is on public State Lands, but the tower is closed as it contains numerous pieces of radio equipment.

visit.trail_note: NY lookout association page: visitors may go to the site, though without the tower there is no view.

corrections.why: The Register, nysffla and Wikipedia all give 67 ft 6 in (20.57 m) for the tower. The 24.4 m figure matches only the 1942 NGS note of about 80 ft overall, which describes the structure differently.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register, nysffla and Wikipedia agree on 67 ft 6 in (20.57 m). The 1942 NGS station note says about 80 ft overall. The story uses the 67 ft 6 in figure, which is the repeated tower height; the NGS figure is noted as a discrepancy.
nysffla says the tower ceased operation at the end of the 1988 season and was officially closed in early 1989; the Register gives 1989 as the decommissioning year. These describe the same closure.

notes_for_editor: Staffing, closure and 1940 build are consistent across NHLR, nysffla and Wikipedia. Elevation differs slightly (NHLR 2,108 ft; Wikipedia 2,106 ft); the record's 642.5 m is kept and not put in facts. The NHLR photo credit (Laurie Rankin, 2012) has no image URL, so no photo added. Not verified: the current owner or use of the radio equipment, and whether any recent visit or closure record exists. Access is inferred from the NHLR closure note; no visit report found.
